hook: Say the same hard thing two ways: rewind any line of a fictional argument, swap a blaming line for an I-statement or a real reflective listen, and watch the other kid's face, reply and the conversation meter change.
outcome: Use I-statements, reflective listening and both-sides plans to work through an ordinary conflict with a peer
sources: CASEL, What Is the CASEL Framework? (Relationship Skills: communicating effectively, listening actively, resolving conflicts constructively), casel.org
I-statements (I-messages): Thomas Gordon, Parent Effectiveness Training (1970); Gordon Training International, I-Messages, gordontraining.com
Active (reflective) listening: Carl R. Rogers and Richard E. Farson, Active Listening (1957), University of Chicago Industrial Relations Center
